findings.claim: the order of the amended steps cannot observe the absent-key no-op the case was amended to cover, so the third assertion passes under the implementation REQ-01-034 forbids

witness.detail: The steps read: 'Set the organization country to PL, then submit an empty value, then submit a body carrying no countryCode key at all' (cases.md:435-436). After the second write the column is null, so the third write answers 200 {"countryCode":null} both when the route no-ops on an absent key and when it clears on one - the shipped organization-country.service.ts:76 clears, and this case as ordered would still pass against it. The Expected Result nevertheless reads 'The third write answers 200 and changes nothing ... a mistyped key must not drop a country the fallback depends on' (cases.md:439-441), and 'changes nothing' is only observable against a stored country.

findings.suggestedFix: Planned around without editing the document: T9 keeps every step the case names and re-sets PL before the keyless body, asserting 200 {"countryCode":"PL"} and a GET that still answers PL. A note rather than a blocker because nothing here is undecided - the rule is settled at spec:359 and contracts:133-134, and only the order of one case's writes is weaker than the outcome it states.

findings.claim: no numbered case covers REQ-01-018 at unit level, and edge case 18's third limb - an unrecognized zone - is asserted by no case at any level

witness.detail: Edge case 18 (contracts:420) states the fallback for three inputs: null, empty, and 'a string the server does not recognize'. The only case covering REQ-01-018 is TC-01-INT-19 (cases.md:414-429), whose three readers are Pacific/Kiritimati, Pacific/Niue and an account whose column is null - the unrecognized limb is in no step. The unit cases cover REQ-01-014/015/016/019 (TC-01-UNIT-02), REQ-01-026/027/040 (TC-01-UNIT-01), REQ-01-028/029 (TC-01-UNIT-03) and REQ-01-001/003 (TC-01-UNIT-04); none names REQ-01-018, so the helpers the contracts require (contracts:213-214) have no case of their own.

findings.suggestedFix: Planned, not blocked: T9 puts the helper assertions - including the unrecognized zone - in the describe block carrying TC-01-UNIT-02, which is the convention round 3 set for a rule whose exports the spec names but numbers no case for (rule 9's country tests sit under TC-01-UNIT-01 the same way). A blocker here would be growing the spec, not refining it; a person adding a numbered unit case for REQ-01-018 is the cleaner close.

findings.claim: two of the three findings that sent this back were already stated in the plan the implementer worked from, so the plan's round-3 wording did not carry them into the diff

witness.detail: T4's round-3 text already read 'AN ABSENT countryCode KEY CHANGES NOTHING ... test the key itself', and T2's already read 'all three are exports of packages/validation/src/time-off-calendar.ts ... Do not restate the en-CA formatting a second time'. The shipped code does neither (organization-country.service.ts:76; the helpers absent, with time-off-calendar.service.ts:410 restating the fallback). Both instructions were written as rules about the whole change rather than as edits at a named line.

findings.suggestedFix: Round 4 restates both at the point of edit - the file, the line, the shipped expression quoted back, the branch that must exist and what it must not do (no update, no log line) - and names the cheapest wrong fix so it is refused rather than discovered: do not make validateStatedCountryCode refuse undefined.
